description: A single exported resolver in packages/email/src/system returns the system email state (disabled, unconfigured, configured) and the resolved provider type from the environment
The resolver reports disabled only when EMAIL_ENABLE is 'false' (trimmed, case-insensitive); unset, empty, 'true' and any other value are not disabled
The resolver reports unconfigured when not disabled and the credential for the resolved provider type is missing (RESEND_API_KEY for resend, EMAIL_HOST for smtp)
SystemEmailProviderFactory.createProvider creates the provider when the state is configured, with EMAIL_ENABLE unset
prdRefs: Design > Readers move to the resolver

description: All docker-compose files pass EMAIL_ENABLE through without a false default
server/entrypoint.sh does not require EMAIL_ENABLE and does not require EMAIL_FROM, EMAIL_PORT or EMAIL_USERNAME when the flag is unset
.env.example, ee/setup/config.ini, compose.env and the getting-started configuration docs describe EMAIL_ENABLE as an optional off switch
ee/helm/workflow-worker values gain an email block (enabled, provider, from, resendApiKeySecret, smtp) with empty defaults
The workflow-worker deployment renders EMAIL_PROVIDER_TYPE, EMAIL_FROM and SMTP variables only when set, and RESEND_API_KEY and the SMTP password as secretKeyRef
The workflow-worker deployment renders EMAIL_ENABLE=false only when email.enabled is false
workflow-worker extraEnv entries can carry valueFrom
The appliance workflow-worker release receives the same system email settings the appliance app release uses
Existing tests that assert the old gate (systemEmailProviderFactory unit test, password recovery integration test, invoiceCalendarDate test env handling) are updated to the new semantics
